BitNet b1.58 runs on HRX

Microsoft's BitNet b1.58 2B-4T, in the TQ2_0 ternary GGUF (1.11 GiB, 2.06 bits per weight), now runs end to end on the Radeon 8060S through HRX. Every node of the graph is on the GPU; nothing falls back to the CPU. Perplexity on HRX is 102.42 against 102.56 on the CPU for the same file, and decode is 123.4 tok/s.

What was measured#

check result
placement every graph node on HRX0, no CPU fallback
perplexity, same file 102.42 on HRX, 102.56 on the CPU
decode, tg128, before the repack 101.6 tok/s
decode, tg128, after the repack 123.4 tok/s (same binary)

The TQ1_0 and TQ2_0 ternary formats were already full mul_mat formats on HRX. What changed is a load-time step: a TQ2_0 file is repacked once, as it loads, onto the packed-ternary layout our decode kernel reads (llama.cpp fork #147). The same kernel already decodes the packed-ternary Bonsai files; BitNet's weights now take the same path, which is where the 101.6 to 123.4 tok/s comes from. The binary is the same before and after; the file is the one Microsoft publishes.

Microsoft's own runtime for these models, bitnet.cpp, ships no AMD GPU path, so this is a way to run the model on this GPU.

How to run it is the usual: 1bit serve -m <bitnet>.gguf picks HRX for the file. The formats the route covers are listed in HRX on the Radeon 8060S iGPU, and the number sits with the other models in Models measured.

Sources: 1bit-MONSTER/llama.cpp #147, HRX, Models measured.
